facts.text: Lo Prado became an autonomous commune on March 17, 1981, after the military government split Pudahuel into three new municipalities.
The area that is now Lo Prado was once called Las Barrancas, a rural zone that opened the road to Valparaíso during colonial times.
In 1968 construction began on the first phase of Santiago’s Metro Line 1, which today reaches Lo Prado’s San Pablo Avenue.
Lo Prado’s Parque Lo Prado is a green pocket that hosts family picnics, sports courts, and weekend walkers every Saturday.
The commune’s name, Lo Prado, echoes its agricultural past, where haciendas and chacras dotted the landscape before urbanization.
Lo Prado’s municipal council is led by an alcalde elected every four years, with the current term running from 2024 to 2028.
